gen-dafont-disorder-gf-inter-tight: Inter Tight is sans-serif with short ascenders and tidy, modern tails. Disorder is best at chaotic shouting, with big lowercase and glyphs set well apart, while Inter Tight is best at holding text in tight, tubelike lines.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-karla: Raw, scattered letters up top, stocky friendly ones below. Disorder is best at thin-looking, unshaded strokes with a chaotic edge, while Karla is best at a tall middle band and gaping c openings.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-liter: Raw and chaotic, each Disorder glyph standing well apart from the next. Liter follows with no stroke contrast at all, plus wide round mouths and strong vertical presence that steady the page.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-martel-sans: Unshaded, constant strokes give Disorder a raw, chaotic look, with glyphs set well apart. And Martel Sans, with generous curve openings and a high mean line, reads smoothly across many lines.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-matangi: Disorder is raw and chaotic, its big lowercase and widely spaced glyphs showing no swelling where curves meet stems. Matangi, twine-like and hefty in the lowercase, gives all that commotion solid footing.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-mozilla-headline: Raw chaos up top, a friendlier voice underneath. What stands out is how Disorder keeps its joins as thin as its stems, while Mozilla Headline stays big-bodied and friendly with a splayed c terminal.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-nobile: Every stroke of Disorder is the same gauge, raw and chaotic. Nobile, with its tight gap between lowercase and caps and open letter mouths, would read crisply over pages of text.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Open and welcoming, with capitals barely above lowercase, this body reads cleanly. Noto Kufi Arabic backs up Disorder, whose pen-like line of constant weight keeps its chaos raw and spaced out.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Disorder is raw and chaotic, a true monoline display face whose lowercase looks big and glyphs sit well apart. Noto Sans Adlam keeps curve endings apart and its c, s, z full.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-noto-sans-bugines: Noto Sans Buginese reads smoothly, its ascenders short and its letter mouths open. Paragraphs of it would flow without fuss, while Disorder, with no stress in any curve, supplies the raw chaos.
